key_insight: Quasi-van der Waals epitaxy of Zn3P2 on graphene significantly improves material quality and grain size, impacting photovoltaic performance.
engineering_relevance: Understanding the relationship between defects and optical properties is crucial for enhancing the efficiency of thin-film solar cells.
method: Utilized metal-organic vapour phase epitaxy (MOVPE) for film growth.
Conducted correlative electron microscopy and cathodoluminescence (CL) analysis.
Compared MOVPE-grown films with those created by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE).
evidence_signal: CL analysis revealed that grain boundaries serve as non-radiative sinks for charge carriers, extending several micrometers into grains.
watch_item: Grain boundaries may lead to detrimental effects on charge carrier recombination, impacting overall device performance.
paper_title: Cathodoluminescence Analysis of Defects and Grain Boundaries in Zn3P2 Thin Films Grown on Graphene by MOVPE and MBE
